requirements.title: IOSTAT= is zero when no error, end-of-file, or end-of-record condition occurs
requirements.definition: Executing an I/O statement with IOSTAT= defines the stat variable with zero if no error, EOF, or EOR condition occurs.

pending.iostat-success-zero: Initialize IOSTAT to a nonzero sentinel, perform a successful internal WRITE or READ with known data, and assert IOSTAT equals zero.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. requirements.title: INQUIRE on an internal-file unit number reports the named positive IOSTAT value
requirements.definition: If a unit number in an INQUIRE statement identifies an internal file, IOSTAT= is defined with the positive processor-dependent value of ISO_FORTRAN_ENV IOSTAT_INQUIRE_INTERNAL_UNIT.

pending.iostat-inquire-internal-unit-positive-na: Use an INQUIRE whose unit number identifies an internal file as specified by the INQUIRE rules, initialize IOSTAT to zero, and assert equality to IOSTAT_INQUIRE_INTERNAL_UNIT and that the value is positive.

requirements.title: Other input/output errors report a positive IOSTAT value distinct from IOSTAT_INQUIRE_INTERNAL_UNIT
requirements.definition: For any other error condition, IOSTAT= is defined with a processor-dependent positive integer value different from IOSTAT_INQUIRE_INTERNAL_UNIT.

pending.iostat-other-error-positive: Establish a nonexistent file name with INQUIRE EXIST=.false., OPEN it with STATUS="OLD" and IOSTAT=, and assert a positive IOSTAT value.
pending.iostat-other-error-distinct-from-inquire: In the same program, separately obtain IOSTAT_INQUIRE_INTERNAL_UNIT through the named constant and assert the other-error status is not equal to it, without comparing either exact number.

requirements.title: End-of-file reports the named negative IOSTAT_END value when no error occurs
requirements.definition: For EOF with no error condition, IOSTAT= is defined with the processor-dependent negative value of ISO_FORTRAN_ENV IOSTAT_END.

pending.iostat-eof-iostat-end: Read beyond a one-record internal file with IOSTAT initialized to zero and assert equality to the named constant IOSTAT_END.
pending.iostat-eof-negative: In the same EOF case, assert the resulting status is less than zero, not any exact negative value.

requirements.title: End-of-record reports the named negative IOSTAT_EOR value when no error or EOF occurs
requirements.definition: For EOR with no error or EOF condition, IOSTAT= is defined with the processor-dependent negative value of ISO_FORTRAN_ENV IOSTAT_EOR.

pending.iostat-eor-iostat-eor: Provoke nonadvancing EOR on a short external formatted record with IOSTAT initialized to zero and assert equality to the named constant IOSTAT_EOR.
pending.iostat-eor-negative: In the same EOR case, assert the resulting status is less than zero, not any exact negative value.
pending.iostat-eor-distinct-from-end: Assert IOSTAT_EOR is distinct from IOSTAT_END by named constants, as required by the separate status alternatives.

requirements.title: Unsupported FLUSH reports a negative IOSTAT value distinct from IOSTAT_EOR and IOSTAT_END
requirements.definition: If IOSTAT= appears in a FLUSH statement and the processor does not support flush for the specified unit, the status is a processor-dependent negative value different from IOSTAT_EOR and IOSTAT_END.

pending.iostat-flush-unsupported-negative: No portable oracle can require a processor to lack FLUSH support for a chosen unit; future tests may guard on observing unsupported FLUSH and then assert only negative status.
pending.iostat-flush-unsupported-distinct-from-e: Under the same guarded unsupported-FLUSH observation, assert the status is not IOSTAT_EOR and not IOSTAT_END; otherwise make no claim.

requirements.title: Exact nonzero IOSTAT numeric values are processor dependent
requirements.definition: The exact positive and negative nonzero IOSTAT values, including the values of the named constants, are processor dependent except for their required sign and distinctness relationships.

accounting.rationale: IOSTAT alternatives mix required signs/named constants/distinctness with processor-dependent exact values.
Portable sign and named-constant equality for internal-file unit inquiry.
Portable positive other-error status and distinctness.
Portable EOF named constant and sign.
Portable EOR named constant, sign, and distinctness from EOF.
Processor latitude for exact nonzero numeric status values.
NOTE gives example EOF/error branching logic and is not normative.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.10.3-12.12: IOLENGTH, error, end-of-record and end-of-file conditions, IOSTAT=, IOMSG=, and restrictions on I/O statements (batch166). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer, accepted with no findings. IOLENGTH's exact count is latitude but its direct-access RECL= suitability is planned; END=/EOR= conditions, IOSTAT_END and IOSTAT_EOR distinctness, zero on success and positive errors are planned portably; IOMSG unchanged on success is planned with a sentinel while condition-message text is never compared. Source accounting only.
